solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Not very great shopping centre is in outskirts of Slough (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the shopping centre and 'is' sit in the outer letters
indicatorNotes.outskirts of: outskirts are the edges of a town, so take only the first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of SLOUGH
a mall is a shopping centre

annotation.surface: A modest shopping mall on the edge of Slough, a town west of London.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'is' is not a link word here; it goes into the box alongside MALL.
annotation.definitionFit: Smallish means fairly small, so not very great.

entries.clue: Snake enters dilapidated housing quietly (7)

indicatorNotes.dilapidated: a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so rearrange the letters
indicatorNotes.housing: the rearranged letters hold P inside them

annotation.surface: A snake slithers into a derelict house without a sound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enters' reads as the snake's verb, but it is the word to be rearranged, and 'quietly' is the musical p that goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: serpent is the older, more literary word for a snake, as in the serpent in Eden.

entries.clue: Delight American showed in games boundlessly (5)

indicatorNotes.showed in: US is shown into the middle of the other letters
indicatorNotes.boundlessly: without its bounds, GAMES loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: GAMES without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: An American delights in showing off at the games.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' wants to be the single letter A; here it is the two-letter abbreviation, sitting inside the trimmed game word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to give pleasure, as a good joke does its listener.

entries.clue: Officers fib, you said, before number of soldiers (11)

indicatorNotes.you said: 'you' spoken sounds like the letter U
indicatorNotes.before: LIE and U come before the rest

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like 'you'
soldier ants: 'soldiers' is a crossword stand-in for ants

annotation.surface: Officers tell lies about how many troops they have.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number of soldiers' reads as a troop count; it splits into a number and an insect, since soldiers are a caste of ant.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: lieutenant is one rank of commissioned officer, in army and navy alike.

entries.clue: I must replace area of tray made of metal (6)

indicatorNotes.must replace: I takes the place of the A

blocks.note: a salver is a serving tray
a = area; this A comes out
goes in where the A was

annotation.surface: An instruction to swap part of a metal tray.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase, as in a silver spoon.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: a silver cup or spoon is one made of that precious metal.

entries.clue: Develop good argument (4)

blocks.note: a row (rhymes with 'cow') is a quarrel

annotation.surface: A healthy argument helps you grow as a person.
annotation.walkthrough: In British English a row, said to rhyme with 'now', is a noisy argument.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a child or a business can be said to develop or to grow.

entries.clue: Concerned about a child’s motives (7)

blocks.note: a son is a child; the apostrophe is ignored

annotation.surface: Worrying about why a child behaves as they do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concerned about' looks like worry but is just RE, as in the heading of a memo.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what drove someone to act are the motives behind it.

entries.clue: Unite opposing sides in graduate club (5)

indicatorNotes.opposing sides in: the two sides of GRADUATE, its first and last letters

blocks.note: to wed is to unite in marriage
first and last letters of GRADUATE

annotation.surface: Rival factions come together in an alumni society.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Graduate club' reads as a society; the club is a golf club, the wedge.
annotation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club for short lofted shots.

entries.clue: Run no further, regularly missing path (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly missing: every other letter goes missing, leaving the even ones

blocks.note: r = run, as in cricket scores
the even letters of NO FURTHER: nO fUrThEr

annotation.surface: A runner who can go no further, having lost the path.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run no further' reads as a runner giving up, but it is R plus a letter pick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the way you take from one place to another is your path.

entries.clue: Tight-fitting garment was first donned by old sailor (7)

indicatorNotes.donned by: a garment donned is worn around you, so LED wraps the rest

blocks.note: to have led is to have been first

annotation.surface: An old sailor was the first to squeeze into a tight garment.
annotation.walkthrough: The garment in the surface is the answer itself; the wordplay reads LE(O TAR)D.
annotation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

entries.clue: Six deliveries a vendor arranged repeatedly (4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters of A VENDOR are put in a new order

blocks.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled

annotation.surface: A vendor sets up the same six deliveries again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests parcels, but these are cricket balls: an over is six balls bowled by one bowler.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: doing something time after time, again and again.

entries.clue: Finally restore the ancient organ (3)

indicatorNotes.Finally: take the final letter of RESTORE

blocks.note: ye is an old spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe

annotation.surface: An instruction to restore an ancient organ, as in a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ancient organ' paints a church instrument; the organ is the eye, and 'the ancient' is YE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: of the body's sense organs, this is the one for sight.

entries.clue: So entertained by act here for evening (9)

indicatorNotes.entertained by: the answer is held within the words that follow

blocks.note: hidden in acT HERE FOR Evening

annotation.surface: A performance is put on here for the evening's entertainment.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre picture hides the answer across four words.
annotation.definitionFit: Therefore and so both mean for that reason.

entries.clue: Cheers monarch is receiving (6)

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks, like 'cheers'

annotation.surface: A monarch is being toasted as the crowd cheers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' suggests a toast, but in British usage both 'cheers' and 'ta' mean thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: Taking and receiving both mean accepting what is given.

entries.clue: Equipment that man installed in empty common room (7)

indicatorNotes.installed in: HE is fitted inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.empty: emptied of its middle, COMMON keeps only C and N

annotation.surface: A man fits equipment in an unoccupied common room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Common room' looks like one phrase and a definition, but only 'room' defines; 'common' is emptied to CN.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the room of a house where food is cooked.

entries.clue: Had success in test — that’s given (6)

blocks.note: first sense: got through an exam
second sense: handed over, as with the salt at table

annotation.surface: Passing the test is taken for granted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's given' reads as 'that's a certainty'; it is the second meaning, handed over.
annotation.definitionFit: Passed means both succeeded in a test and handed to someone.

entries.clue: Cursorily read old papers in retirement, consuming some beer (3,4)

indicatorNotes.in retirement: retiring means going back, so O and ID are turned round
indicatorNotes.consuming: the turned letters take PINT inside them

blocks.note: a pint is a measure of beer

annotation.surface: A retired person leafs through old papers over a beer.
annotation.walkthrough: The retiree in the surface is a reversal: retiring goes back, so the old papers are read backwards before the beer goes inside them.
annotation.definitionFit: To dip into a book is to read bits of it casually.

entries.clue: Equilibrium not entirely lost as I swerved (6)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: hidden in loST AS I Swerved

annotation.surface: A driver who swerved nearly lost their balance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swerved' hints at an anagram, but the answer runs straight through the words.
annotation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of balance where nothing changes.

entries.clue: Noted date suspect set off (9)

indicatorNotes.suspect: suspect means unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

annotation.surface: A recorded date for when a suspect left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun, a person under suspicion; here it is an adjective telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bomb that has been triggered to explode has been set off.

entries.clue: Stink after gutting fish all around harbourside (5)

indicatorNotes.after gutting: a gutted STINK loses its insides, leaving S and K
indicatorNotes.all around: the whole string is turned around

annotation.surface: Gutting fish leaves a stench all around the harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' is not an order word here: 'after gutting' means once the smell word is gutted. Its remains go first, the fish second, and the whole lot is turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Docks are the part of a port along the harbourside.

entries.clue: Strike old boy back with power (3)

indicatorNotes.back: going back means travelling in reverse, so the old boy's letters are read the other way

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil

annotation.surface: Hitting an old boy back hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' is British for a former pupil of a school, shortened to OB.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a bop is a light blow, so to deliver one is to strike.

entries.clue: Upset, cry about conclusions of you being fake (5)

indicatorNotes.Upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so read them backwards
indicatorNotes.about: SOB goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.conclusions of: the last letters of YOU and BEING

blocks.note: last letters of YOU and BEING

annotation.surface: Someone upset and in tears about being called a fraud.
annotation.walkthrough: S(UG)OB is built first and then the whole thing is turned over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bogus doctor or a bogus claim is a fake one.

entries.clue: I’m surprised, overwhelmed by expenditure for presenting duo (2-5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'duo' names the pair; CO-HOSTS names its members

indicatorNotes.overwhelmed by: OH is swamped by, and so inside, COSTS

annotation.surface: A pair of TV presenters shocked at how much they have spent.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation lands just after the first letter of the spending word, splitting it.
annotation.definitionFit: Two people who present a show together are its co-hosts.

entries.clue: One dodging certain fare, say, aboard transport (5)

indicatorNotes.aboard: EG is on board, inside, the vehicle

blocks.note: a van is a means of transport

annotation.surface: A fare dodger riding a bus or train without paying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price; it is food, and a vegan dodges meat and dairy.
annotation.definitionFit: A vegan avoids certain food, namely animal products.

entries.clue: Go astray by end of corporate function (4)

indicatorNotes.end of: take the last letter of CORPORATE

blocks.note: to sin is to go morally astray

annotation.surface: Misbehaving at the office party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporate function' paints an office event; the function is the trigonometric one.
annotation.definitionFit: A mathematical sense: one of the trigonometric functions, alongside cosine and tangent.

entries.clue: Cook reposes with second coffee (8)

indicatorNotes.Cook: to cook the books is to rework them, so rearrange the letters

blocks.note: s = second, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A cook relaxing with a quick coffee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a person resting; it is the verb telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.
